decisionsTitle: The volunteers' list can be public: the name and the role of the confirmed volunteers who ticked, only once the privacy notice says so
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-19 08:30**, on the event's volunteers (§754, §768): «On the volunteers form I want extra settings so that I can have "invite only volunteer" "private vs public lists of volunteers" "Brașov Runners only" volunteers.» The first and the third are the previous decision's (who may offer); this one is the second: **the volunteers' list stays the team's alone, or is shown on the event's page, by name, for the people who say so.** And, on seeing the card: «Asta ar trebui să fie collapsed, ca și condițiile de participare.» Amends §754 (the offer «nu apare pe lista publică»; «Lista voluntarilor … o văd doar organizatorii») and extends §143 and §396 — the disclosure rule of CLAUDE.md — to volunteers.

**A public name is a disclosure.** Until now nothing public named a volunteer: the list was the editor's card, the CSV and the badges. This makes it possible, behind two ticks and a gate, and changes nothing for an event that does not tick it (the default, on every event, after the migration).

**Decision — two ticks, one per side.** Migration `0172` (an expand: three columns, no reader to break): `events.volunteers_list_public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, `event_volunteers.list_opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` and `event_volunteers.list_opt_in_notice_version integer NULL` (the notice the tick was given under).

- **The club's tick**, in the «Voluntari» card under «Arată public câți voluntari mai sunt necesari»: **«Lista voluntarilor e publică pe pagina evenimentului»**, the house's one-press `TickButton` (a submit drawn as the checkbox; the card's own form, never the editor's save; `setVolunteersListPublic`, audited as `event.volunteers_list_switched`, no version bump). While it is on and the notice in force does not describe the list, the card says so in a sentence with a link to «Documente legale».
- **The volunteer's tick**, on the public form of every way in (the page's own form, a member's, an invited person's): **«Vreau să apar pe lista publică a voluntarilor»**, a `CheckboxField` with one help line («Pagina evenimentului arată doar numele tău și rolul dat de organizatori, după ce te confirmă. Poți cere oricând, în scris, să fii scos de pe ea.»), off by default, never required, never kept in the sealed draft (it is the person's own act each time, like the consent). **It is drawn only where it promises something true** — the club's tick on **and** the notice describing the list (`VolunteerOffer.listTick`) — and **the server asks again** (`submitVolunteer`): a tick posted while either is missing is dropped, never stored and never refused (the person agreed to nothing that was described; the sign-up itself is unaffected).
- **The organizers' record of it**, for a person they enter or edit («Adaugă un voluntar de mână», «Modifică»): the same words as a `CheckboxField` in the person's boxes, «Vrea să apară pe lista publică a voluntarilor», with its help («Bifează doar dacă persoana ți-a spus că vrea, de preferat în scris. Numele tău rămâne în jurnal.»). **Recorded by the staff member like the paper agreement of §758**: the audit row (`volunteer.added` carries `listOptIn: true`; `volunteer.edited` names the box among its fields) names who, never the person. It is drawn while the notice describes the list and for a person already ticked (so a tick can always be cleared); **the service refuses a new tick without the notice** (`VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `listOptIn`) and a post that leaves it alone changes nothing. A newly recorded tick writes the notice version in force into `list_opt_in_notice_version` — **never** into `privacy_notice_version`, which is the record of the notice a public sign-up consented under (GDPR art. 7(1)) and stays empty on a row the club entered: an organizer who ticks the box for a person who signed up under an older notice leaves that record alone. A sign-up that keeps the tick writes the same version into both columns; a cleared tick keeps no version. The art. 15 export shows both.
- The row on the card says **«Vrea pe lista publică»** (`StatusChip`, the `wantsList` glyph — a word and a picture, never colour alone) for anyone ticked: it names the wish, not a state, because the page names a person only once they are also confirmed, the club's tick is on and the notice describes the list.

**The gate (`domain/public-list.ts`, pure, tested without a database).** The page draws the card only when all of these hold: the club's tick is on; **the event still takes volunteers** («Primește voluntari» is the master switch — off, nothing about volunteers is public, as it always hid the form); the event is published, public (never a members' event, §552) and the volunteers' rows still exist (the card goes on the day the retention sweep may take them, thirty days after the event's start, §754, and the static page is made again then); **the privacy notice in force describes the list** (`{{volunteersList}}`, in every language, and `{{volunteers}}` with it); and at least one volunteer may be named. A volunteer is named only if they are **confirmed** (a person nobody accepted, or who withdrew, is not «the team» — and, as the participant list shows the confirmed, a default that discloses less), **an adult**, **ticked**, and ticked under **a notice that described the list — the first such version or a later one** (`findFirstVolunteersListNoticeVersion`, §421's line, the notice-version rule of «Vin!» §811 and the results §808, read from the tick's own `list_opt_in_notice_version`): a tick given under an older notice agreed to nothing this describes, and that person is counted, never named. A null version (no notice behind the tick) never qualifies. **A volunteer under eighteen (an age under 18, or a guardian on the row) is counted and never named**, whatever they ticked: the guardian's acceptance covers the agreement (§768) and the notice says the guardian's data are used only for that consent; a name on a public page is another disclosure, and §323 keeps a minor's socials off every public list. This stays until the owner and the lawyer decide how a guardian consents to it (open point 6).

**What shows (`VolunteersList`, a Server Component, after the volunteers' callout and before «Condiții de participare»).** A native `details`, **closed on arrival, in the shape of «Condiții de participare»** (the owner: «collapsed, ca și condițiile de participare» — the title a real `h2` inside the `summary`, a glyph, the count: «Voluntarii (5)»): the names in the order of the sign-ups with the role the organizers **gave** each, if any (the roles a person only ticked are their wish list and never shown), and «și încă N voluntari» for the confirmed who did not tick (a count only, in the three forms of Română). When nobody may be named it shows nothing — except the one sentence **«Echipa de voluntari se formează.»** when the volunteers' offer is open, so a page that asks for people does not look empty. **Never an address, a telephone number, a city, a birth date, a message, a note, the guardian**: the read (`readPublicVolunteersList`) selects the name, the state, the tick, the tick's notice version, the role's two names and — only to keep a minor off — the age and the guardian's name, and the cached value is exactly `{ count, named, others }` (a test in `tests/privacy/public-surface.test.ts` pins the select and greps the JSON for an address; AGENTS.md §10.10 carries the rule). It is filed in the public cache under `places` and `events` — the tags every write to the people expires (`changeVolunteer`, a confirmation, a deletion, the retention sweep's removal, now followed by `revalidatePublicContent("places")`) — and, being under `places`, keeps no saved copy (§281: a withdrawn name must not outlive the request). While the database is away the card is left out. The wrapper carries `data-nosnippet`: names stay out of search snippets.

**The notice.** The privacy notice's template gets a merge field **`{{volunteersList}}`** (the tick's own words, quoted, read from the catalogue the form reads) in the volunteers' paragraph of section 5: what the page then shows — the name and the role given, nothing else — after the organizers confirm, until the offer is deleted (thirty days after the event's start, section 7); the others as a count; basis the person's consent (art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), withdrawn by writing, the name leaving the page; and «nu apare pe lista publică» now says **«a participanților»**, with «Lista completă a voluntarilor, cu adresa și telefonul» for the organizers' list. The gate is the §562 / §613 / §765 / §811 pattern: `noticeDescribesVolunteersList` (uncached, for the sign-up, the organizers' record, the card and `/admin/tasks`), `cachedVolunteersListDescribed(now)` and `cachedFirstVolunteersListNoticeVersion()` (for the page — the §808 trio). A notice approved before says none of it, so nothing public happens until the club approves one from the new template; `/admin/tasks` carries the row **`volunteersListNotice`** («Textul pentru lista publică a voluntarilor») while an upcoming event has the list public and the notice is silent, done by itself when a notice naming it takes effect, never blocking. **A lawyer reads the paragraph first.**

**What travels.** Like «Cine se poate oferi» and unlike «Primește voluntari», the club's tick travels with a duplicate and with every date of a repeat (`copiedEventValues`) and with the event's JSON file (the volunteers block's `listPublic`, written only when it is on — the mirror of `rsvpEnabled` — so a file of an event that never made the list public stays readable by the release before, and applied to a new event through the card's own service, audited). No volunteer, no tick of a person and no «Primește voluntari» travels with it: the copy shows nothing until the club ticks the offer, people sign up and are confirmed, and a notice describes the list.

**Open for the owner and the lawyer.** (6) **A minor is counted, not named**; naming one would need the guardian's explicit consent to the list and a sentence in the notice saying so — the owner and the lawyer decide whether the club wants that. (1) **Only the confirmed are named and counted**; the brief of this change said «ticked volunteers», and an offer nobody accepted is, on the participant list's own logic, not on the list. If the owner wants a name the moment someone ticks, it is one line in the read. (2) «și încă N voluntari» and the title's count are a public number about volunteers and do not ask «Arată public câți voluntari mai sunt necesari» (§773, which is about how many a *role* still needs); the owner decides whether they should. (3) Whether the consent a staff member records for a person they entered suffices for a public name (the template says so; a lawyer reads it). (4) The thirty days: the name leaves the page with the offer, thirty days after the event's start. (5) The «Voluntari» card's tick stays on after «Primește voluntari» goes off, but the page shows nothing then — the master switch wins.

**Refused.** A new role or table for the list; naming a person who did not tick, whatever their state; naming a confirmed person under a notice that did not describe the list (counted instead); showing the roles a person only ticked; showing a city, an age or a count of roles; one tick for both the form and the card (the volunteer's consent and the club's choice are two acts); the tick on the form while the club's list is private (it would promise what the page does not do); refusing a sign-up for a tick that cannot be kept (it is dropped instead); a toggle button for the club's tick (`TickButton` is the owner's rule of 2026-10-14); an open-on-arrival card (the owner asked for it closed); the cached page serving a name after the offer's deletion (the sweep and the thirty-day line both end it).
changelogLine: - **The volunteers' list can be public** — a new tick in the «Voluntari» card, **«Lista voluntarilor e publică pe pagina evenimentului»** (off by default), adds a card **«Voluntarii»** to the event's page, closed on arrival like «Condiții de participare»: the name and the role given of each confirmed adult volunteer who ticked **«Vreau să apar pe lista publică a voluntarilor»** on the form (or whom the organizers recorded), «și încă N voluntari» for the rest (a volunteer under eighteen is only counted) — only once the privacy notice describes it (`/admin/tasks`: «Textul pentru lista publică a voluntarilor»). Never an address or a telephone number. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given an event's volunteers (§754), when its page renders, then a volunteer is named only if they are CONFIRMED, an adult (a minor is only counted), ticked «Vreau să apar pe lista publică a voluntarilor» (or the organizers recorded it, audited with their name) under a privacy notice that described the list — the first such version or a later one — and the event's club tick «Lista voluntarilor e publică pe pagina evenimentului» is on, the event still takes volunteers and the notice in force describes it (`{{volunteersList}}`, in every language); every other confirmed volunteer is a count, «și încă N voluntari», and no address, telephone number, city, birth date or role merely ticked is ever read; the card is a fold closed on arrival and goes thirty days after the event's start (2026-10-19, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event's «Voluntari» card, when the club ticks «Lista voluntarilor e publică pe pagina evenimentului» (a one-press tick, off by default, audited, never the editor's save), then the public form asks the optional tick «Vreau să apar pe lista publică a voluntarilor» only while the notice in force describes it, the organizers' entry records it only under that notice (refused naming the box otherwise, and a tick can always be cleared), the row says «Vrea pe lista publică», the notice version of the tick is kept apart from the sign-up's consent record, `/admin/tasks` carries the row `volunteersListNotice` while an upcoming event has the list public and the notice is silent, and the tick travels with a duplicate, a repeat and the event's file but no volunteer does (2026-10-19, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the volunteers' list can be public on the event page: names and roles, only of those who ticked, once the notice describes it
